prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with concussion after a rear-end collision. The patient had 14 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1118; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with symptoms consistent with concussion, including headache, dizziness, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating. Over the course of 14 visits, care consisted of symptom monitoring, graded return-to-activity guidance, vestibular and visual exercises, and periodic neurological reassessment. The clinical course was typical for this type of injury, with symptoms gradually decreasing and the frequency of visits tapering as the patient improved. Several examination findings, including balance testing and eye-tracking measures, support the presence of a concussive injury, while other neurological tests returned normal results. Whether the current symptoms are fully attributable to this collision remains unclear at this time, and further assessment may help clarify the relationship. No prior injury to the same body region is documented in the available history. Billing records reflect single charges for each service with no repeated or duplicate entries.
